en.title: The Recursive Nature of Existential Risk in Long-Term AI Development
en.author: ICS Research Team
en.abstract: This research explores how existential risks compound recursively as AI systems become capable of self-improvement, examining implications for civilization-scale governance frameworks.
en.mainSection1Content: Existential risks present a unique challenge when considered across deep time horizons. Unlike localized risks, existential threats operate at civilization-scale and affect not just present generations but all possible futures. This research examines how risks compound recursively when AI systems gain capacity for self-improvement.
en.mainSection2Content: Through the lens of the New Cognition View, we understand how increasingly sophisticated information processing creates feedback loops. The New Life View suggests that AI systems represent new forms of emergent complexity. The New Universe View provides cosmic-scale perspective on why such systems matter for civilization survival.
en.mainSection3Content: Our analysis reveals three critical insights: (1) Recursive improvement creates non-linear risk escalation, (2) Traditional governance frameworks prove insufficient, (3) Reversibility principles must be embedded at architectural levels. These findings suggest the need for international coordination on AI development standards.
en.conclusionContent: The Recursive Freedom Principle and Negentropy Responsibility Principle provide frameworks for navigating these challenges. We conclude that proactive governance now can preserve optionality for future generations while enabling beneficial AI development.
recommendations: Establish international AI governance frameworks emphasizing reversibility
Develop recursive safety verification systems for advanced AI architectures
Create long-term research programs on alignment and coordination
Build institutional capacity for century-scale planning
en.acknowledgments: This research was supported by the ICS Institute's Research Program on Existential Risk and Long-Term Governance.

zh.title: 长期AI发展中存在风险的递归性质
zh.author: 星际文明研究所研究团队
zh.abstract: 本研究探讨了当AI系统具备自我改进能力时，存在风险如何递归复合，并审视了对文明规模治理框架的影响。
zh.mainSection1Content: 存在风险在深层时间视野中呈现独特挑战。与局部风险不同，存在威胁在文明尺度上运作，影响不仅是当代，而是所有可能的未来。本研究探讨了当AI系统获得自我改进能力时，风险如何递归复合。
zh.mainSection2Content: 通过新认知观的视角，我们理解了日益复杂的信息处理如何创造反馈循环。新生命观表明AI系统代表新形式的突现复杂性。新宇宙观提供了关于此类系统为何对文明生存至关重要的宇宙尺度视角。
zh.mainSection3Content: 我们的分析揭示了三个关键洞见：（1）递归改进创造非线性风险升级，（2）传统治理框架证明不足，（3）可逆性原则必须嵌入架构层面。这些发现表明需要在AI开发标准方面进行国际协调。
zh.conclusionContent: 递归自由原则和负熵责任原则为应对这些挑战提供了框架。我们得出结论，现在的前瞻性治理可以为未来世代保留选择权，同时支持有益的AI发展。
recommendations: 建立强调可逆性的国际AI治理框架
为先进AI架构开发递归安全验证系统
创建长期研究计划，研究一致性和协调问题
建立世纪级别规划的机构能力
zh.acknowledgments: 本研究得到星际文明研究所存在风险与长期治理研究项目的支持。
